A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MERGETUNE research work and complete 20-page material, including Appendix A. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original MERGETUNE experiments on base-to-novel, cross-dataset, and distribution-shift generalisation, plus backbone evaluations and ablations in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including benchmark results in Tables 1–6 and supplementary analyses in Tables 7–11 and Figures 3–5.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same continued fine-tuning procedure, second-order surrogate, LMC regularisation, initialization, and inference model. The final objective in Equation 9 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 recognition datasets, four ImageNet distribution-shift variants, and ObjectNet under the same base-to-novel, cross-dataset, domain-generalisation, and robust fine-tuning tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding main-text and appendix tables, including the PEFT baselines, TIES, DARE, weight ensembling, and VRF. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.1 retain the same class splits, 16-shot settings, metrics, preprocessing, model configurations, and training schedules. The additional-backbone and ablation protocols also match.

E4.justification: Both contain identical hyperparameter and initialization analyses, interpolation-count sensitivity, endpoint-loss and loss-component ablations, connectivity analysis, and extended-training checks for over-merging (Section 5.6 and Appendix A.3).

E5.justification: Both state that reported results are averaged over three random seeds. No run-count information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout Tables 1–11 and Figures 1–5. For example, Table 1 retains CoOp+MERGETUNE's average HM of 77.24, and Table 4 retains the ensembled E2E-FT result of 62.90 Avg-D.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same interpolation definitions, LMC formulation, Taylor derivation, near-stationarity assumption, and isotropic-Hessian approximation. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about recovering forgotten pretrained knowledge through model-agnostic continued fine-tuning, avoiding pretraining-data replay, and improving generalisation without architectural changes.

C2.justification: Interpretations of knowledge recovery, loss-component contributions, interpolation behavior, computational tradeoffs, and resistance to over-merging are unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, pseudocode, NVIDIA 3090 hardware disclosure, and training-cost discussion remain identical. Both provide the same code-repository link; no resource-access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to VLM adaptation, model merging, and robust fine-tuning remains identical.

P1.justification: v3 adds the running text 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body wording, terminology, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The publication header and first-page version marking change the page margins. All page bodies render identically, including the five figures, eleven tables, equations, captions, and their placement.

improvement.justification: v3 changes publication and version markings while retaining identical scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information, including the appendices. These administrative presentation edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
